findings.title: Word-hint requests have no raw utility byte admission
findings.expected: An outside utility request has an explicit size bound; reuse the existing InputText domain, preserving normal last-word behavior. This is a coding-rule bound, not an altered cryptographic-format requirement.
findings.observed: The AUD-032 defect is corrected in the exact final source manifest; see remediation evidence.
findings.impact: Avoidable linear scanning and copied/transferred data before a small answer; no measured exhaustion, remote attack or secret leak. Native typed-line front ends already cap their input; raw/browser callers expose this gap.
findings.recommendedFix: Settle the public hint input contract and use library-owned admission in the raw binding and pre-encode class paths; expose/reuse needed metadata. Do not silently truncate text or alter KDF parameters. Preserve typed: MhfeSecret, including Uint8Array; the current string-only InputTextBoundary.read is insufficient for that public contract. Passwords metadata needs the selected utility-limit contract.
findings.requiredVerification: Exact max/max+1 byte controls with multibyte input; normal hints/completions; stable error code; pre-copy/worker ordering; document any source API signature/limit changes.

Include excessive visible-line retry and full refused-line draining; preserve genuine I/O, EOF/cancel and script-mode semantics.

findings.title: Single wish entries remain unbounded after the corrected array-count guard
findings.expected: Bound one outside entry and its raw whitespace/text before join, encoding, transfer or full trimming/scanning; preserve bounded count and valid word semantics.
findings.observed: The AUD-032 defect is corrected in the exact final source manifest; see remediation evidence.
findings.impact: Caller-supplied linear scanning/copying persists with a small final answer. No exhaustion, remote exploit, secret disclosure or incorrect cryptographic output was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Choose a library-owned per-entry/utility-text byte domain, enforce it at direct/raw and class pre-copy boundaries, and document its compatibility. Do not silently trim an unbounded outside value before admission.
findings.requiredVerification: Entry max/max+1 UTF-8 byte controls with ASCII/multibyte whitespace; ordinary chosen/excluded positives; exact errors before join/encoding/worker; retain the existing array-count/getter/message controls and all direct/raw refusal tests.
findings.history: Original AUD-028-API005 retained. AUD-030 verified the distinct browser array-count/getter/message correction; that correction is still supported. This is the previously unclosed single-entry/whitespace variant, not a new count regression.

findings.baselineObserved: One valid chosen/excluded word padded to 8,192 and 8,193 UTF-8 value bytes reaches actual raw semantics and full class transport, for ASCII and U+2003 padding. The wire adds one framing newline, giving 8,193/8,194 bytes. No exact supported wire maximum is asserted by this probe.
findings.implementedFix: Each chosen/excluded word value is bounded before copy/scan and wire framing; exact-limit Unicode and caller storage remain supported.

findings.title: Incomplete final startup reports can admit an operation
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The normal trusted current Rust producer emits a complete report; no spontaneous producer omission or attacker path without package-code control was demonstrated. This is a malformed-protocol resilience defect.
findings.expected: A fresh class with no cached passes must reject a partial/mismatched final startup report before starting its actual requested operation. Legitimate cached/tier-filtered and explicit failed-trap reports remain valid.
findings.observed: The AUD-032 defect is corrected in the exact final source manifest; see remediation evidence.
findings.impact: A malformed final response can turn absent self-check evidence into page-only success. No failing cryptographic result, ordinary-producer omission, remote exploit or compromise was established.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate required completed tier/component identity and multiplicity before updating shared passed-check state or admitting the operation. Do not use every([]) or silently remove required absent ids as success.
findings.requiredVerification: Fresh empty/partial/missing-id/extra-id/duplicate/mismatched reports refuse before operation and do not poison cache; retain complete real positives, shared verified-cache skip, startup/full tier differences and failed trap reports without ids. Native set.ids() includes full-only items before tier filtering, so requiring every declared id at startup is incorrect.
findings.baselineObserved: After a complete actual five-component report succeeds, each of three fresh module identities receives an incomplete final report: empty components without ids, empty components with all actual startup ids, and the first component with all ids. All three dispatch the actual class inspectContainer request and resolve from a synthetic stand-in-worker operation response. The real Rust inspectContainer computation is not executed by this probe. The strict assertion exits 1.
findings.implementedFix: Requested-tier catalogs must be complete across streamed results and the verified cache captured before a run; partial reports cannot add cache passes or dispatch work. Full Argon2 checks retain independent per-build known answers.

findings.title: The ordinary PTY cancellation control assumes text survives a combined Ctrl+C write
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A required ordinary Unix terminal gate currently fails on this Linux host. This is a test-driver prerequisite failure; native macOS execution is not claimed.
findings.expected: Establish that the fixture was visibly rendered before checking private display/erasure and cancellation. Keep strict non-vacuous assertions and the expected cancellation status/terminal restoration.
findings.observed: The AUD-032 defect is corrected in the exact final source manifest; see remediation evidence.
findings.impact: The required gate cannot currently establish its cancellation/concealment assertion and blocks acceptance. No secret echo/leak or product cancellation failure was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Send synthetic text separately, synchronize on its rendered private-screen fixture, then send Ctrl+C and retain the current strict oracle. Do not weaken the assertion or disable Python assertions.
findings.requiredVerification: A real Unix PTY demonstrates the fixture first and passes Ctrl+C status, private display, erasure and terminal restoration. Include a repeated/race control; verify the applicable native platform separately. The audit wrapper must refuse Python -O before spawning.
findings.history: The earlier strict-oracle correction under AUD-028-BLD006 remains valid; it exposed this distinct driver timing/precondition defect.
findings.baselineObserved: The driver sends SECRET plus Ctrl+C in one write. Unix ISIG/default flushing may discard unread text before the application displays it. After 15 earlier printed scenario summaries, the ordinary group exits 1 with AssertionError: Ctrl+C: the expected password was not shown. The earlier cancellation status 130 and terminal-settings assertions pass.
findings.implementedFix: PTY cancellation waits until typed text is visibly present before Ctrl+C; the strict oracle checks raw and normalized leakage outside the private screen.

findings.title: Linux work-area dump exclusion ignored refusal and lacked readback
findings.reproduction: The old hash-pinned CLI reaches its first secret prompt after the preload shim refuses MADV_DONTDUMP.
findings.expected: Apply and verify every whole page before use; refusal/unavailable metadata is a typed fatal failure.
findings.observed: Baseline failure retained; corrected exact source passes the stated regression.
findings.impact: A library host need not share the CLI process-wide core policy. The previous madvise result was ignored and no whole-range dd readback was required. No actual dump/secret-recovery exploit was run.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply and verify every whole page before use; refusal/unavailable metadata is a typed fatal failure.
findings.requiredVerification: Tiny kernel/parser/logical-C-extent tests, startup classification, and the same actual PTY fault against the fresh CLI.

findings.title: Evidence recorder accepted nonfinite timeouts
findings.reproduction: recorder-controls.py supplies nan, inf, -inf, zero and negative deadlines and a marker-writing child.
findings.expected: Reject invalid timeouts before starting a command.
findings.observed: Baseline failure retained; corrected exact source passes the stated regression.
findings.impact: The inherited precursor accepted nan/inf; no such timeout occurs in the retained remediation receipts.
findings.recommendedFix: Reject invalid timeouts before starting a command.
findings.requiredVerification: All invalid cases refuse without creating the marker.

findings.title: Forced recorder termination could return success
findings.reproduction: A tiny child sleeps after installing a SIGTERM handler that exits zero.
findings.expected: Keep exitCode=0 but return a nonzero wrapperExitCode for the forced stop.
findings.observed: Baseline failure retained; corrected exact source passes the stated regression.
findings.impact: A SIGTERM handler can exit zero after a wall timeout. The actual child status must be retained separately from the wrapper failure. No false-green forced stop occurs in the retained precursor receipts.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep exitCode=0 but return a nonzero wrapperExitCode for the forced stop.
findings.requiredVerification: The timeout control requires wall-timeout, child zero and nonzero wrapper status.

findings.title: Recorder leader exit could abandon a live process group
findings.reproduction: Independent red controls use a signal-resistant child with both a waiting and an immediately exiting leader.
findings.expected: Observe the leader without reaping its PID; monitor live same-group members and stop them on timeout.
findings.observed: Baseline failure retained; corrected exact source passes the stated regression.
findings.impact: The old stop helper skipped a resistant child when the leader exited after SIGTERM; the main loop also stopped monitoring after an ordinary leader exit. This concerns local audit tooling, not product child-process behavior.
findings.recommendedFix: Observe the leader without reaping its PID; monitor live same-group members and stop them on timeout.
findings.requiredVerification: Both controls require no live surviving child and a failed wrapper; normal success stays zero.

findings.title: CLI pin wrapper could report success with optimized assertions
findings.reproduction: The retained earlier wrapper under PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1 returns zero after its child refuses to run with assertions disabled.
findings.expected: Refuse optimized Python before hashing or starting a child; require a successful child and stable ELF hashes during ordinary runs.
findings.observed: Baseline parent exit0 despite child refusal is retained; the corrected public wrapper exits1 under both -O and PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1, and ordinary real PTY controls pass with identical before/after ELF hashes.
findings.impact: A local evidence helper could falsely appear successful under an unusual interpreter setting. The earlier actual normal CLI logs contain executed controls; they are not invalidated as vacuous by this variant.
findings.recommendedFix: An explicit sys.flags.optimize refusal before the first side effect.
findings.requiredVerification: Environment/flag refusal controls and actual public wrapper PTY execution with before/after ELF equality.

limitations: This is a focused remediation acceptance, not a new full semantic audit or proof of universal CORE conformance.
Actual Windows console and macOS native/package acceptance remain unexecuted on this Linux host.
No new cached/uncached canonical Docker pair, signed release verification or paid CI dispatch.
No full-cost 2 GiB vector replay; bounded known answers and reduced-cost cryptographic controls are distinct.
Compiler-complete public export/trait roster gap from AUD-032 is retained; source bindings do not close it.

The browser verifier rebuilt the debug CLI without remap flags: older native runtime evidence belongs to ELF666969..., and current hash-pinned CLI/dump controls belong to ELF d916a5.... Both versions and their separate receipts remain retained.

Linux dump exclusion is checked at allocation, not proof against privileged later changes; procfs is required. Rounded page policy can persist in the allocator after free until unmap. Other native protections are unchanged.
Byte-view ownership preserves caller storage, not immutable content under a concurrent writer.
Complete startup catalogs detect inconsistent producer reports, not an adversarial producer forging a full pass.
Finite regressions cannot prove total physical erasure, arbitrary terminal emulator behavior, all scheduling cases or absence of every defect. Sampled memory is not a kernel cap.
Historical precursor natural-leader process-group completion is not retroactively certified. Recorded invalid timeouts/forced false-green statuses were checked and absent.
